title: 长歌行
author: 佚名（汉乐府）
intro: Garden plants glowing in spring, rivers that never flow back west — and then the famous warning: “If you don’t work hard while you’re young, you’ll grieve in vain when you’re old.” Chinese parents still quote it to their children.
analysis: 这首诗从园子里的葵菜写起：早上叶子上挂着露水，等着太阳出来把它晒干。春天把阳光和雨水洒给大地，万物都闪着光彩，生机勃勃。可是诗人马上担心起来：秋天一到，花和叶子就会变黄、枯萎。接着又写到江河——成百条河流都向东流进大海，什么时候见过它们流回西边呢？植物有盛衰，流水不回头，都是在说时间一去不返。最后两句才说出道理：“少壮不努力，老大徒伤悲。”年轻时不努力，老了只能白白后悔。前面用景物打比方，最后点明道理，这种写法叫“托物言理”，道理就不显得生硬。这两句今天已经成了中国人最常说的劝学名言之一。
analysisEn: The poem begins in a garden: green mallow plants hold morning dew on their leaves, waiting for the sun to dry it. Spring pours out warmth and rain, and everything glows with life. But the poet immediately worries: when autumn comes, the flowers and leaves will turn yellow and wither. Then he turns to rivers — a hundred of them all flow east into the sea, and who has ever seen one flow back west? Plants that bloom and fade, water that never returns: both are pictures of time that cannot be won back. Only in the last two lines does the poem state its point: “If you don’t work hard while young and strong, you will grieve in vain when old.” Using images first and saving the lesson for the end makes the advice feel natural rather than preachy — a technique Chinese teachers call “using things to express a truth” (托物言理). Those last two lines have become one of the most quoted sayings about study and effort in Chinese; parents and teachers still use them today.
background: This is an anonymous Han dynasty yuefu song, preserved in Guo Maoqian’s Collection of Yuefu Poems (12th century) under “Songs in Concert” (相和歌辞). “Long song” (长歌) probably names the style of singing — long, drawn-out notes — rather than the length of the poem.
pronunciation: 朝露的“朝”读 zhāo（早晨）；晞 xī（晒干）；焜黄 kūn huáng；华叶的“华”读 huā（同“花”）；少壮的“少”读 shào（年轻）。华叶衰的“衰”现行教材和通行读本注 shuāi；为押韵（与晞、辉、归、悲同韵）旧读 cuī；此处采用 shuāi。
version: 采用通行的教材文本（出自宋郭茂倩《乐府诗集》卷三十《相和歌辞·平调曲》），全诗十句，网站按两句一行排版，共五行。

lines.zh: 青青园中葵，朝露待日晞。
lines.rhythm: 青青/园中葵，朝露/待日晞
lines.py: qīng qīng yuán zhōng kuí, zhāo lù dài rì xī
lines.lit: Green, green, the mallows in the garden; the morning dew waits for the sun to dry it.
lines.en: Green mallows fill the garden, their morning dew waiting for the sun.
lines.tts: 青青园中葵，招露待日晞。

lines.zh: 阳春布德泽，万物生光辉。
lines.rhythm: 阳春/布德泽，万物/生光辉
lines.py: yáng chūn bù dé zé, wàn wù shēng guāng huī
lines.lit: Warm spring spreads its kindness; all things give off light and colour.
lines.en: Warm spring pours out its kindness, and everything shines with life.

lines.zh: 常恐秋节至，焜黄华叶衰。
lines.rhythm: 常恐/秋节至，焜黄/华叶衰
lines.py: cháng kǒng qiū jié zhì, kūn huáng huā yè shuāi
lines.lit: I often fear the autumn season will arrive, when flowers and leaves turn yellow and wither.
lines.en: Yet I always fear the coming of autumn, when flowers and leaves fade to yellow.
lines.tts: 常恐秋节至，昆黄花叶衰。

lines.zh: 百川东到海，何时复西归？
lines.rhythm: 百川/东到海，何时/复西归
lines.py: bǎi chuān dōng dào hǎi, hé shí fù xī guī
lines.lit: A hundred rivers flow east to the sea; when will they return west again?
lines.en: A hundred rivers run east to the sea — when have they ever flowed back west?

lines.zh: 少壮不努力，老大徒伤悲。
lines.rhythm: 少壮/不努力，老大/徒伤悲
lines.py: shào zhuàng bù nǔ lì, lǎo dà tú shāng bēi
lines.lit: If you do not work hard when young and strong, when old you will grieve in vain.
lines.en: Work hard while you are young, or grieve for nothing when you are old.
lines.tts: 哨壮不努力，老大徒伤悲。

words.note: 古代常吃的蔬菜，不是今天的“向日葵”。
朝读 zhāo。书面语，也比喻短暂的生命。
现代汉语仍用，如“光辉的形象”。
节：季节。今天不说“秋节”，说“秋天”“秋季”。
形容草木枯黄，今天不用。
少读 shào，现代汉语“少年”。
古义是年老；今天“老大”指排行第一或头儿。

imagery.name: 葵
imagery.zh: 春天里青青的葵菜，象征生命最好的时光——青春。
imagery.en: Fresh green mallows in spring stand for the best season of life: youth.

imagery.name: 露
imagery.zh: 朝露很快就会被晒干，暗示美好的时光短暂易逝。
imagery.en: Morning dew dries quickly in the sun — a hint that good times are short.

imagery.name: 水
imagery.zh: 百川东流不再西归，比喻时间一去不复返。
imagery.en: Rivers flowing east and never back west: time that, once gone, never returns.
